-79.34938,43.79673.name: Seneca Polytechnic
-79.34938,43.79673.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, March 2026
-79.34938,43.79673.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, March 2026. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-51.16999,-30.01168.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: http://www.insemine.com/. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere.

-72.20557,41.17920.name: Foreign Animal Disease Diagnostic Laboratory (FADDL) at Plum Island Animal Disease Center (PIADC)
-72.20557,41.17920.state: P.O. Box 848 Greenport, N.Y. 11945, United States
-72.20557,41.17920.company: U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS)
-72.20557,41.17920.desc: A BSL3+ laboratory, operational. Run by U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS). It is categorised as a public health laboratory, working on animal health. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

121.56540,25.03300.name: Food and Drug Administration — GM food registration
121.56540,25.03300.desc: Taiwan requires registration and labelling of engineered foods and maintains a public register of approved events. Its labelling threshold is stricter than the American approach and looser than the European one, which places it in the middle of a global argument usually described as two-sided.

-90.20000,38.62800.name: Bill & Melinda Gates Agricultural Innovations (Gates Ag One)
-90.20000,38.62800.desc: The foundation’s agricultural vehicle, funding crop development for low-income countries. Philanthropy is among the largest funders of putting engineered organisms into the ground there, so the usual test of whether farmers want a product never happens.

-81.30090,26.12240.name: Rewilding and genetic rescue — Florida panther precedent
-81.30090,26.12240.desc: Texas cougars were introduced into the remnant Florida panther population in 1995, reversing inbreeding effects and tripling the population. It worked, it is decades old, and it required no biotechnology — which is the comparison any engineered genetic rescue has to make and rarely does.

9.96000,56.46000.name: VikingGenetics
9.96000,56.46000.desc: A Nordic farmer-owned cattle cooperative running genomic selection across Danish, Swedish and Finnish herds. Cooperative breeding puts the genetics in the hands of the farmers who use them, and it produces the same narrowing of the gene pool as the corporate route, because selection intensity is what narrows it rather than ownership.

2.31100,48.84000.name: Institut Pasteur
2.31100,48.84000.desc: A private foundation doing public work on infectious disease, with a network of institutes across thirty countries, many in places with no other high-capacity laboratory. That network is where a great deal of pathogen sequencing actually happens, and it long predates any international arrangement for it.

11.34350,44.49450.name: Declarations of interest — the people on the panel
11.34350,44.49450.desc: Every member of a scientific panel assessing an application must file a declaration of interests, and in the EU those declarations are published alongside the panel’s opinion, naming past employers, funding and consultancies. Most regulators worldwide have an equivalent requirement and a good many publish it. It is the most direct answer to ‘who decided this and what else are they involved in’, and it sits one click from the assessment itself.
